verdict_note: Nothing found that breaks the build. Admission comes before the first byte for both item kinds. A refusal partway through the queue leaves earlier outputs and receipts consistent. The pinned digest covers every shipped preset by construction. Fix F1 and F2 before the bundled run: both are small and both touch the export_sequence refusal path that the run has to prove. F3 (PNG colour) needs a lead ruling: either a cut named in the receipt, or a fix before landing. F4 to F7 are LOW and can ride along.

findings.severity: MEDIUM: wrong refusal on an existing command (export_sequence regresses for shipped presets)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/timeline/export_media.rs:564 (export_prepare: `recipe_record(&request.preset_id, &self.user_recipes()?)?`); src/view/delivery.rs:325 and :485 (same eager parse in delivery_add and delivery_request); src/view/timeline_export.rs:648 (recipe_record), :796-:810 (user_recipes refuses the WHOLE entry: over 8 MiB, schema, any bad record, duplicate id, or an id equal to a shipped preset)
findings.what: Every sequence export parses the export_recipes entry before it checks whether the id is a shipped preset, so the whole entry has to be readable first. Any unreadable entry now refuses export_sequence, the Export Media form, the CLI export-sequence verb and delivery sequence items with export_recipes_invalid, even for studio.* presets that never look at user recipes. At base the same export succeeds. This is also a change in export_sequence's refusal order: export_recipes_invalid now comes before unknown_preset and codec_unavailable.
findings.scenario: Open a package whose studio/export_recipes entry this build cannot read. Examples: a newer writer's hsk.studio.export_recipes@2, a body over 8 MiB (see F2), or a user recipe id that a later build ships as a preset (timeline_export.rs:808 then rejects the whole entry). Run export-sequence --preset studio.dnxhr.lb.mov: it exits 1 with export_recipes_invalid. At eb17fad6 the same command writes the file.
findings.fix: Resolve shipped ids first and parse the entry only when export_preset(id) is None, for example recipe_record(id, || self.user_recipes()) with a lazy closure, at all three call sites. Add a delivery_queue test: a corrupt entry still exports a shipped preset, and a user id refuses export_recipes_invalid. Because export_sequence's refusal order changes, run the process tests that drive it (lead_questions 2).

findings.severity: MEDIUM: lost capability; a document wedged after save and reopen (hostile or extreme input through the typed rows)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/delivery.rs:704-738 (export_recipe_save stores user_recipes_entry(&recipes) with no size check) and :747 (export_recipe_delete parses the entry first); src/view/timeline_export.rs:635 and :796 (reader refuses a body over 8 MiB); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness/export_recipes.rs:17 and :36 (the store accepts up to 32 MiB); crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/export_recipe.rs:349-353 (text values up to 4096 bytes, no character rule) and :660-:670 (json_str writes each char below 0x20 as 6 bytes); export_parameter_rows.rs rows "0" (Opaque, Other) and "ADBEAudioChannelConfiguration" (Path, Audio) take text values and are not credentials
findings.what: The writer and the reader use different bounds. Save checks only the 256-recipe count and stores any body up to 32 MiB. Every read refuses a body over 8 MiB. The code comment at :632-:635 itself says 256 maximal recipes exceed 8 MiB. Two 4096-character text parameters made of control characters serialize to about 49 KB per recipe, so about 170 such recipes (fewer than 256) cross 8 MiB. The save that crosses the line returns success. After that, export.recipes, recipe_save, recipe_delete and every user-recipe export refuse export_recipes_invalid, and so does every shipped preset export while F1 stands. After save and reopen there is no undo step, and recipe_delete cannot repair the document because it parses the entry before deleting.
findings.scenario: Run export.recipe_save from studio.dnxhr.lb.mov with parameters {"0": 4096 x "\u0001", "ADBEAudioChannelConfiguration": 4096 x "\u0001"} for ids user.1 through user.171. Then save the package and reopen it. export.recipe_delete user.1 refuses export_recipes_invalid.
findings.fix: In export_recipe_save, refuse with a typed code (export_recipes_full) when user_recipes_entry(&recipes) is longer than MAX_USER_RECIPES_BYTES, before set_export_recipes runs. Lower harness-core MAX_EXPORT_RECIPES_BYTES to the same 8 MiB. Add a boundary test.

findings.certainty: READ (code); UNVERIFIED (the visible tone difference: whether composite decodes a shape fill to linear was not traced)
findings.severity: MEDIUM: wrong answer, or a cut that the output does not state (lead ruling)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/timeline_export/composition.rs:827-844 (PngModule::encode: the clamped sample times 255 or 65535, no transfer function, icc: None); src/view/delivery.rs:290-292 (composition items render in the linear sRGB working space, BlendSpace::LinearLight); src/view/timeline_export/render_queue.rs:239-244 (output_color_space rec709|bt709|srgb and embed_color_space are accepted; the PNG branch never reads them); src/view/render.rs:742 (the viewer applies the sRGB OETF for display); src/view/doc_export.rs:369, :425, :544 (the document PNG export applies the OETF and embeds SRGB_V4_ICC); harness-core motion_commands.rs default_module (a new png_sequence module has embed_color_space true and output_color_space rec709)
findings.what: The PNG sink writes linear-light working-space samples straight into 8- or 16-bit codes and adds no colour chunk. The module record meanwhile says rec709 with embed_color_space true. Readers treat an untagged PNG as sRGB-encoded, so the frames do not match the viewer or the document PNG export of the same pixels. Nothing on the receipt or in the RenderNotes says the COLOUR group was ignored. STU-MOT-122a requires a colour mismatch to surface before the render. The lane notes record the choice ('written as rendered, like the MOV path'), but neither the product output nor the receipt states it. Composition MOV items run through delivery inherit the same reading of linear samples as R'G'B' (UNVERIFIED).
findings.scenario: The test fixture fills straight [0.8, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5] and the PNG holds 204, 26, 26, 128, untagged. A reader shows sRGB 204. If 0.8 is a linear value, the viewer shows 231 (render.rs encode(0.8)).
findings.fix: Option (a): for srgb, rec709 or an unset space without preserve_rgb, apply doc_export's oetf to straight RGB (premultiply after encoding when color is premultiplied), leave alpha linear, and pass icc Some(SRGB_V4_ICC) when embed_color_space is true. Option (b): refuse typed (output_png_colour_unconverted) or put a RenderNote on the receipt until (a) lands. A silent cut should not land.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/motion_commands.rs:1027-1077 (template_module) and :1080 (queue_apply_template); harness-view render_queue.rs:267-270 (an AV1 module is rebuilt as Av1Settings { quantizer, ..default() })
findings.what: (1) An AV1 recipe maps only its quantizer. speed, bitrate and max_keyframe_interval are dropped without the template_not_mapped refusal that the function applies to parameters, scope, targets and filters. A recipe stored by another producer (STU-IO-110: recipes are portable) encodes with the defaults while the op record names that recipe. Through Studio's own rows a user recipe can only inherit studio.av1.mp4's settings, which equal Av1Settings::default(). (2) The module keeps its output_path, channels and color. Applied to a png_sequence module (renders/x.png) or to a MOV module with an MP4 recipe, it produces a MOV written to x.png, or an MP4 container named .mov.
findings.scenario: composition.queue_add format png_sequence output_path renders/x.png, then queue_apply_template with user.hq (from studio.dnxhr.hq.mov), then queue_set_module channels rgb, then delivery.run. The receipt reports renders/x.png complete, and that file holds a QuickTime DNxHR stream.
findings.fix: Refuse template_not_mapped when the AV1 speed, bitrate or max_keyframe_interval differ from what the module can store. Refuse template_format_unsupported on a png_sequence module, or reset its channels and color. Refuse (or rewrite) when the output_path extension does not name the target container.

findings.certainty: UNVERIFIED (Win32 path normalization of trailing dots and spaces, 8.3 names)
findings.severity: LOW: clobbered output with two receipts that both claim it (only when overwrite is true)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/delivery.rs:176-190 (relative, collision_key) and :413-436 (delivery_collisions compares output_path patterns, not PNG frame names)
findings.what: The collision key folds only ASCII case and the path separator. Paths that are equal on Windows still pass as two outputs: a trailing dot or space (out.mov and out.mov.), an 8.3 alias, or a sequence output equal to one of a PNG module's expanded names (renders/title_0000000.png next to the pattern renders/title.png). Without overwrite the no-clobber publish catches this. With overwrite, the later item replaces the earlier item's file, and both receipts say complete and name it.
findings.scenario: Add a sequence item output a.mov and a sequence item output a.mov. with overwrite true, then delivery.run. One file remains, and two complete receipts name it.
findings.fix: In relative(), refuse segments that end in '.' or ' ', and Windows device names (CON, NUL, COM1 and so on). In the collision check, refuse any output that matches <stem>_<7 digits>.png of a queued PNG pattern.

findings.severity: LOW: allocation that grows with the frame count (bounded at 4,000,000 per module)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/timeline_export/composition.rs:945 (one String per written frame); src/view/delivery.rs:645 (json!(r.artifacts)), :408 (receipts.clone() into DeliveryState), :409 (returned again); harness cli.rs execute_deliver prints it
findings.what: A PNG receipt lists every file. A maximal module (4,000,000 frames, allowed by PngModule::check) holds about 4M Strings in the receipt, again as a serde Value, again as the stored copy and in the returned run, and once more for each PNG module of each item. That is hundreds of MB per module, and delivery.receipts serializes all of it again.
findings.scenario: A png_sequence module over a 3-hour, 60 fps composition (648,000 frames) builds receipts of roughly 100 MB or more in three copies.
findings.fix: Name the pattern, the first and last number written, and the count (frames_written and last_written already exist in PngSequenceReceipt::json). Keep the full list out of the receipt.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/delivery.rs:461-480 (every Err from export_sequence_with becomes refused, job null); src/view/timeline/export_media.rs:535-552 (Err export_worker after admission: spawn failure, worker panic or no receipt, each after settlements.fail)
findings.what: When a sequence item was admitted and then failed in the worker, the receipt says outcome refused with job null, and counts.refused counts it. The admission actually settled failed (export_worker), and after a panic frames may already have been served. The module docs define 'refused' as a refusal before any frame.
findings.scenario: The hsk-export-media thread fails to spawn, or panics, during delivery.run. The receipt reads refused, while job_counts records one failed job.
findings.fix: Make export_sequence_with return the settlement it made (or a typed post-admission error), and write outcome failed with code export_worker and the job settlement into the receipt.

Confirm the bundled filter names them, with a freshly built examples/studio-harness.exe for the process tests.

PngModule::check refuses frames > 4,000,000, the same comparison reel uses (reel export.rs:672), so exactly 4,000,000 frames is accepted. The brief's hostile example says 4,000,000 is refused. Which is meant?

Composition items: should delivery_collisions refuse the WHOLE run when one queued render queue item has since been removed (render_queue_item), or should that be the item's own refused receipt, as the module docs say for build refusals?
checked: Admission before any byte: sequence items run export_prepare (no file I/O), then AdmittedExportQueue::submit, then the worker. Composition items run delivery_build (tile copy and records, no file I/O), then one submit per reel module and JobAdmission::admit per PNG module, all before the hsk-delivery thread starts. A pre-run cancel cancels the handle or token at registration (delivery.rs:143-158), so reel settles canceled and the PNG sink stops before frame 0.

A refusal partway through the queue: each item's receipts are appended independently (delivery.rs:395-404). A refused module is counted as a SharedFrames consumer but never reads, and the cache is bounded by the per*frames <= DEFAULT_SHARED_CACHE_BYTES check whenever consumers > 1. Settlements zip in submission order (job_admission.rs settle). The PNG jobs are settled on both the worker-ok and the worker-fail paths.

Pinned digest afbdd389: ExportPreset::recipe at base was already studio_recipe().resolve(os) (presets.rs:118-120). Shipped presets carry no Integer parameters (export_recipe.rs:692-721: only ADBEVideoTargetBitrate as a Float, for H.264 and HEVC), so job_from_recipe's source checks skip them, and it rebuilds ExportJob with all eight fields moved unchanged (export_recipe.rs:775-784). Every preset's job is therefore field-identical to base, and one digest plus this construction covers all six. The codec_unavailable code and detail are unchanged (Writer(e) maps to e.to_string() in both).

relative(): rejects '', more than 1024 bytes, any ':' (drive letters, ADS), a leading '/' or '\\' (root, UNC, \\?\), and any '.' or '..' segment. A symlink or junction that already exists under the save root can lead outside it, but a package cannot create one. export_sequence still accepts absolute paths (unchanged from base), and the delivery queue never reaches that branch.

User recipes: unknown or missing fields are refused (FIELDS count), does_video and does_audio must agree with the codec, numbers go through set_parameter, the 453-parameter and 64-target limits are hit early, duplicate ids and shipped-id shadows are refused, json_f64 keeps floats as floats on the round trip, a codec the build lacks lists available false and delivery_add refuses codec_unavailable, and the entry stays byte-identical when no recipe exists (None).

PNG publish: create_new temp, then hard_link for no-clobber; the fallback rename runs only after a symlink_metadata check, mirroring reel. Every write failure names the frames already written (test png_sequence_names_the_frames_written_when_a_write_fails).
